svg.title: How a passkey protects the signing key
svg.desc: The passkey's PRF output is stretched with HKDF into an AES-256-GCM key that wraps the Ed25519 signing key. The wrapped copy is stored in the browser, on the server and in an optional backup file; on another computer the same passkey rebuilds the same wrapping key and unwraps it.

svg.text: The wrap is useless without the passkey: only the passkey can produce the PRF output that unlocks it, so anyone may hold a copy.

text.font-family: DejaVu Sans, Liberation Sans, Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: Another passkey adds another wrap of the same key. A backup file (Advanced options) encrypts the key under a passphrase instead.
